Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b10/review-experiment-x4gteh10/call-9f8933be5c0e44f3b73665fd850a065e/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
    print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(reader.pages))
print('METADATA',reader.metadata)
out=Path('tmp/pdfs')
out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
text='\\n\\n'.join(f'===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n{page.extract_text()}' for i,page in enumerate(reader.pages))
(out/'manuscript.txt').write_text(text)
print(text[:25000])
PY"

strengths: The joint treatment of ID and OOD confidence for random forests and neural networks has an identifiable audience in uncertainty estimation and tabular learning. The shared polytope construction provides a useful connection between these model families.

For a fixed fitted model with positive Gaussian variances and a positive additive floor, Proposition 2 gives a sound, transparent explanation of convergence to the empirical class prior as distance increases without bound. This behavior does not require OOD training examples.

The evaluation covers six simulations, 45 OpenML datasets, controlled image shifts, and vision experiments with two encoders. The per-dataset appendix and Euclidean-versus-geodesic comparisons provide useful detail beyond aggregate results.

The reported vision results demonstrate a potentially useful tradeoff. In Table 1, KDN reduces CIFAR-100 OCE from 0.47 to 0.12 and SVHN OCE from 0.44 to 0.08, while CIFAR-10 accuracy decreases from 98.06% to 97.45%. Table 4 also reports improved ID MCE relative to the parent model.
weaknesses: Necessary: distinguish prior reversion from statistical calibration. Equation (1) stipulates the training prior as the desired OOD prediction; it does not establish that this is the correct conditional label distribution under a shift. Moreover, OCE in Equation (18) checks only maximum confidence, so it does not fully evaluate even the stipulated target on imbalanced datasets. For example, priors (0.6, 0.3, 0.1) and predictions (0.6, 0.1, 0.3) yield zero OCE despite different probability vectors. Narrow the calibration claims to the demonstrated confidence behavior, or provide evaluation and assumptions that support the stronger interpretation.

Necessary: limit the scope of the guarantee. Proposition 2 concerns distance tending to infinity for a fixed fitted model; it establishes neither calibration throughout finite OOD regions nor accurate ID posteriors. The vision implementation adds another limitation: distance in the original image space need not produce distance in the encoder's feature space, where the Gaussians are fitted. The manuscript should make this distinction explicit and restrict its whole-feature-space claims accordingly. The hypersphere experiments support distant-input behavior but do not establish general behavior near the ID distribution.

Necessary: correct the probabilistic interpretation of the construction. Equation (3) treats piecewise-affine network outputs as unnormalized class-conditional densities, although logits can be negative and do not determine class-conditional densities. The positive constant in Equation (6) also makes the resulting functions nonintegrable over an unbounded feature space. These issues do not invalidate the normalized confidence score or its tail limit, but the manuscript should present it as a scoring construction unless a valid density interpretation is supplied.

Necessary: provide enough experimental detail to reproduce and assess the results. Missing information includes the number of repetitions and meaning of uncertainty bands, the OpenML training/calibration/test allocation at each sample size, the search range and objective for k, and important vision training and baseline settings. The pseudocode also does not explicitly implement the exponentiation in Equation (15). Confirm the reported b = exp(-10^-7), which is approximately 1, and explain its scale relative to the Gaussian scores. Appendix C additionally assigns identical Gaussian mixtures to both XOR classes, contradicting the nontrivial classification experiment shown.

Necessary: qualify the baseline conclusions and improve statistical reporting. ODIN is designed for ID/OOD discrimination; its OCE alone does not establish its effectiveness as a detector. Explain how its scores, temperature, and perturbations were used, and either evaluate discrimination when making detection claims or limit conclusions to the chosen prior-reversion objective. Several Table 1 MCE values are rounded to 0.00 with uncertainty 0.00, making the claimed calibration differences difficult to assess. Report sufficient precision and define the uncertainty estimates. These unresolved issues concern support for the current claims, rather than a requirement for state-of-the-art performance.

Optional: a simple Gaussian-mixture or KDE baseline with the same additive floor would help isolate the value of the learned partitions. Runtime and memory measurements would also help readers judge the practical cost of the pairwise fitting procedure. These would strengthen the paper but are separate from the necessary corrections above.
